picks.what: View near Rouen, painting (Metropolitan Museum of Art)
picks.why: color oil sketch; the city’s church towers appear through the trees at right; best of a thin period

picks.why: the classic panorama: river, islands and the cathedral spire; frame and caption cut

gaps: P0: nothing. P2: no independent view (all Merian views carry the date 1620).
notes: P1 alternative: #5 (also #3/#4, #10–#13) Merian’s large panorama ‘Rothomagus Rovan 1620’ (black and white; the plate is dated 1620, later reissued in Topographia Galliae 1657–63, so not used for P2); #1/#2/#8 Braun and Hogenberg vol. 3 bird’s-eye plan (1581). Skipped #17 ‘Vue de Rouen, about 1830’: the cathedral with a tall spire and the market boats look like Amiens, and Rouen had no spire between 1822 and the 1870s. Skipped #30 Pissarro: the ‘1920’ is the British Museum accession number; the etching is from the 1880s. Skipped #29 (date only ‘20th century’). #9 is a flat plan.
